speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand the cause of the swelling and pain in your right ring finger, can you tell me when the symptoms first started and if you have experienced any recent injury or trauma to that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That mechanism of injury strongly suggests a "jammed finger," likely involving a ligament sprain or a fracture. To narrow this down, can you tell me if you are able to fully straighten and bend the finger, or if there is any specific position that causes sharp pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint with pain at that location is highly suggestive of a Jersey Finger, which is an avulsion of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon. I need to confirm if there is a palpable gap or retraction of the tendon belly in your palm or forearm.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal X-ray rules out a fracture, so the issue is likely soft tissue. Can you confirm if you feel a distinct gap or bulge in your palm when you try to make a fist, indicating the tendon has retracted?

text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information, but it doesn't clarify the physical exam findings we need to confirm the diagnosis. Please answer my previous question: do you feel a distinct gap or bulge in your palm when you try to make a fist, indicating the tendon has retracted?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of numbness or tingling helps rule out nerve involvement. To confirm the diagnosis of Jersey Finger, I need to know if you have a palpable gap or retraction of the tendon in your palm when attempting to flex the finger.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound showing normal findings is unexpected for a complete tendon avulsion, so we must consider a partial tear or a different pathology. Please describe the exact location of the most intense pain and whether you can actively flex the finger at all, even if weakly?

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound was normal, which makes a complete tendon rupture less likely, but the inability to actively flex the DIP joint remains the key finding. Can you tell me if you can actively bend the very end joint of your finger, or does it stay straight no matter how hard you try?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient continues to evade the direct question regarding active flexion, so I must rely on the established clinical history of inability to flex the DIP joint following a hyperextension injury, which is pathognomonic for this condition despite the confusing ultrasound result. DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Flexor Digitorum Profundus Avulsion)
